title: Find the Value of the Partition
summary: Given a positive integer array nums, divide it into two non-empty arrays nums1 and nums2 to minimize the partition value.
statement: Given a positive integer array nums, divide it into two non-empty arrays nums1 and nums2 to minimize the partition value. The partition value is the absolute difference between the maximum element of nums1 and the minimum element of nums2.
constraints: Split nums into two nonempty groups.
A split value is the absolute difference between the groups’ maximum and minimum values.
hints: Sort values so every group boundary is visible.
The optimum separates the sorted sequence between two adjacent values.
Return the smallest adjacent sorted difference.
Any two-group separation has a crossing adjacent sorted pair no wider than its extreme gap, and cutting there attains it.
editorial: Any two-group separation has a crossing adjacent sorted pair no wider than its extreme gap, and cutting there attains it.

tests.explanation: Separating values at an adjacent sorted gap of one attains the minimum.
The only split separates ten and one, giving nine.
